READ: top-level directory listing. OBSERVED: see listing; no further files needed for the ideation answer. REASONING: the unused positions I can defend are (a) curved *encoding/assignment geometry* through geodesic chord midpoints rather than codebook updates or radial ranks, and (b) parallel transport of the residual. I will combine them into one mechanism: behaviour-ordered geodesic chord cell per RQ level, residual transported from the curved chord midpoint to the origin. OPEN: finalise equations, safeguards, cost at 24556 items x 24 steps x 3000 epochs.

IDEA: BChordPT-RQ | TITLE: Behaviour-ordered geodesic-chord RQ cells with residual parallel transport (Poincare) | MECHANISM SUMMARY: each RQ level picks the nearest atom a* by Poincare distance, picks a behavioural partner b* = argmax of the previous-epoch atom-level directed transition flow restricted to the M geodesic nearest neighbours of a*, places the level cell centre at the exact geodesic midpoint m* = GeoMid(a*,b*) (Klein-model midpoint), emits a* as the SID token and recentres the level error at the origin by parallel transport: p_{l+1} = exp_0(PT_{m*->0} log_{m*}(p_l)). Behaviour-off sets b*=a* (recovers classical hyperbolic RQ with residual recentred at origin); geometry-off replaces distance/midpoint/exp-log/transport by Euclidean ones (arithmetic mean centre, plain subtraction). COST: +8 geodesic distances, 1 midpoint, 2 log/exp and 1 Lorentz transport per item per level over a 256-atom nearest search => ~5% per-step overhead; one KxK scatter-add per level per epoch over the training transition nnz => <1% of an epoch; ~0.75 MB extra state; no extra epochs, no sweep constants (M=8=sqrt(|C|)/2, alpha=1/N_items, tangent clip atanh(0.95), curvature fixed -1). SAFEGUARDS: ball-norm clip 0.95, acosh argument clamp, empty/zero flow row -> b*=a*, index tie-break, straight-through argmax (no gradient through F or MNN). OBSERVABLES: level-2/3 tokens of gold items shift toward behaviourally linked atoms, prefix predictability and transition adjacency diagnostics recorded (never gated), Stage3 test_recall@10 judged against 0.065. RECORDED AS THE FULL ANSWER BELOW.

IDEA: BChordPT-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-ordered geodesic-chord cells with parallel-transported residuals: the RQ level centre is the geodesic midpoint of the nearest atom and its behaviour-chosen partner
MOTIVATION: In an RQ-VAE the SID hierarchy is built greedily: level l takes the nearest atom, level l+1 refines the leftover error in a frame that knows nothing about where users actually go next. Items that are behaviourally adjacent (one is a frequent successor of the other) often end up in different level-1/level-2 cells whose geometry was fixed by pure reconstruction, so the generator has to memorise transitions that the prefix hierarchy could have made easy. The problem is therefore the *cell geometry and residual frame* of each prefix level, not the codebook means.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds changed codebook updates (successor-weighted Frechet means), per-level curvature control, radial behaviour ranking, Lorentz profile smoothing, cones, successor boosts and branching MoE. This idea changes none of those: the codebooks keep the plain VQ objective, the curvature is fixed, and there is no behaviour loss. What changes is (i) that a level's quantization *cell* is the pair (nearest atom, behaviour-chosen partner) and its centre is the exact hyperbolic geodesic midpoint of the pair, and (ii) that the next level's residual is obtained by *parallel transport* from that midpoint to the origin instead of from the chosen atom. Behaviour acts as a discrete switch on the cell's second vertex; curvature acts as the geodesic midpoint and the transport. Neither alone reproduces the residual frame.
CHANGE: At each RQ level the nearest atom a* is joined with the partner b* that carries the largest training transition flow among the M geodesic-nearest atoms of a*; the level cell centre becomes m* = GeoMid(a*, b*) and the residual fed to level l+1 is log_{m*}(p_l) parallel-transported from m* to the origin. SID tokens are still the atoms, so the prefix sequence changes because every downstream level sees a behaviour-and-curvature-defined residual frame.
SPECIFICATION: Poincare ball of fixed curvature -1, radius clipped at 0.95; L=3 levels, |C_l|=256, dim d=128. Epoch e: (1) forward-pass all 24556 training items to get hard assignments for each level; (2) build per-level atom flow F_l (256x256) by scatter-add of the directed item-transition counts over the current assignments and row-normalise; (3) train with, for each item and level: a* = nearest atom in C_l; N(a*) = the M=8 geodesic nearest atoms of a*; b* = argmax_{b in N(a*)} F_l[a*,b] (b*=a* if the row is empty); m* = geodesic midpoint; token_l = a*; residual point p_{l+1} = exp_0(PT_{m*->0}(log_{m*}(p_l))) clipped. b* and the flow are constants (no gradient), a* uses the straight-through estimator as in the baseline VQ. Loss is the unchanged baseline VQ + commitment + reconstruction encoder/decoder loss.
COST: Per step (batch 24556/24 ~ 1023 items), per level: 8 extra geodesic distances for N(a*) (the |C_l|=256 nearest search is unchanged), 1 Klein midpoint, 2 log/exp maps, 1 Lorentz parallel transport, 1 tangent-norm clip -> roughly 10k extra scalar-op groups per level, about 5% over the ~786k distance evaluations a step already does; three levels -> ~5-8% wall-clock over 3000 epochs. Per epoch: one scatter-add of the transition non-zeros (order 1e6) into 3 matrices of 256x256 plus row normalisation, i.e. a few milliseconds, well under 1% of an epoch. Extra state: 3 x 256 x 256 floats (~0.75 MB). No e

xtra epochs, no extra forward passes, no sweep.
HYPOTHESIS: If the residual frame of a prefix level is shared by behaviourally linked atoms, then items that are frequent successors inside the same prefix will land in cells whose deeper levels refine them with a common geometry, so the level-2/3 tokens of a gold item become predictable from its prefix. Observable as: (a) the level-2/3 token of gold items moves toward the tokens of their training successors relative to a behaviour-off run's assignment statistics, (b) the recorded prefix-predictability / transition-adjacency diagnostics rise while reconstruction stays within the baseline band, (c) Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single frozen run.
RISKS: If the behaviour argmax picks far-away partners inside N(a*), m* drifts off the data mass and reconstruction degrades before the codebook adapts, making the hierarchy noisy. If the flow matrix is stale (rebuilt once per epoch from the previous epoch's assignment) it can oscillate in early epochs. Deep levels may collapse to a small radius near the origin because every residual is recentred there. If transitions are dominated by popularity hubs, many items share one b*. If Stage3 recall is flat, it is impossible to tell within one run whether the drift or the staleness is responsible (no ablations are run).
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transition mass aggregated to the currently assigned SID atoms of each level (a popularity-implicit signal, since raw co-occurrence counts are used without global normalisation beyond the per-row transition probability and the per-row flow normalisation).
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the Stage-2 training split only. For every training session, count ordered pairs (i -> j) for each consecutive step and each skip-1 step within the session; row-normalise to T_ij = n_ij / sum_j n_ij, drop rows with fewer than 2 outgoing events. Once per epoch, with the previous epoch's hard level-l assignments A_l (item -> atom), compute F_l[a,b] = sum_{i in a, j in b} n_ij, then F_l[a,:] /= max(sum_b F_l[a,b], eps) and smooth with alpha = 1/N_items (add-alpha to every entry) so cold atoms are not infinite-penalty. The matrix is recomputed in the epoch loop, never per step, and never differentiated.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition counts, the assignment matrix and the flow matrices are built exclusively from the Stage-2 training interactions; validation and test interactions are never read during RQ-VAE training, and the item vocabulary/atom set is fixed from training items only. The flow matrices are frozen buffers detached from the graph, so no validation signal can enter a codebook, an assignment or a SID; the Stage-3 protocol only consumes the frozen SIDs and its own training split.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = -1 (Poincare ball of radius 1, points clipped to norm <= 0.95). Operations: Poincare geodesic distance d_P; exact geodesic midpoint via the Klein model (k = 2u/(1+|u|^2), k_m = (k_u+k_v)/2, m = k_m/(1+sqrt(1-|k_m|^2))); logarithmic map log_m; exponential map exp_0; parallel transport PT_{m->0} on the Lorentz hyperboloid in closed form.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside quantization, at the assignment/residual step of every RQ level of the Stage-2 RQ-VAE: the cell centre (midpoint) and the residual frame (transport) are curved quantities, used before the level-l+1 nearest-atom search and before the reconstruction decoder.
COUPLING PATH: One pathway per item per level: geodesic nearest

atom a* -> geodesic neighbour set N(a*) -> behaviour flow row F_l[a*,:] selects b* -> curved midpoint m* = GeoMid(a*,b*) -> curved residual log_{m*}(p_l) transported to the origin -> p_{l+1} -> level l+1 token. Removing behaviour collapses b* to a* and m* to a*, which changes p_{l+1} and therefore every deeper token; replacing the curved operations by Euclidean ones changes the neighbour set, the midpoint and the transported residual, so the same flow row selects a different partner and a different residual. Both are inside the single residual computation, not beside it.
COUPLING EQUATION: a*(x) = argmin_{a in C_l} d_P(p_l(x), a); b*(x) = argmax_{b in N_M(a*(x))} F_l[a*(x), b]; m*(x) = GeoMid_P(a*(x), b*(x)); p_{l+1}(x) = exp_0( PT_{m*(x)->0} ( log_{m*(x)}( p_l(x) ) ) ); token_l(x) = a*(x).
OBSERVABLES: (1) SID assignment: the level-2/3 token distribution of gold items and the number of distinct deeper prefixes attached to each level-1 token change relative to a pure-reconstruction geometry. (2) Prefix behaviour predictability: the probability that a gold item's actual next item lies under the prefix predicted by its own prefix chain, recorded per epoch. (3) Transition-adjacency and coherence diagnostics recorded, never used as a gate. (4) Stage3 test_recall@10 is the judgement, against 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: b* := a* for every item and level, so m* = a* and p_{l+1} = exp_0(PT_{a*->0}(log_{a*}(p_l))), i.e. classical hyperbolic RQ residual with the flow matrices present but unused; this switch exists as a config flag and is not trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: d_P -> d_E, GeoMid_P -> arithmetic mean (a*+b*)/2, log/exp/transport -> identity, so p_{l+1} = p_l - m*, while the behaviour flow still selects b* among the 8 Euclidean nearest atoms; this switch exists as a config flag and is not trained in this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full mechanism of COUPLING EQUATION, trained once on the frozen budget (3000 Stage-2 epochs, four cards, frozen Stage-3 protocol, no early stopping) and judged by Stage3 test_recall@10.
SPEC EQUATIONS: 
Per level l, item x with current point p_l (p_1 = encoder output, ball-clipped):
  a* = argmin_{a in C_l} d_P(p_l, a)
  N(a*) = top-M atoms of C_l by d_P(a*, c), M = 8 = sqrt(|C_l|)/2, always containing a*
  b* = a* if sum_{b in N(a*)} F_l[a*,b] == 0 else argmax_{b in N(a*)} F_l[a*,b]
  Klein: k_u = 2a*/(1+|a*|^2), k_v = 2b*/(1+|b*|^2), k_m = (k_u+k_v)/2, m* = k_m/(1+sqrt(1-|k_m|^2))
  r = log_{m*}(p_l) = (1/|k_m|) * atanh(|k_m|) * (p_l - m*) * (1 - |p_l|^2) / ((1 - <p_l,m*>)^2 + |p_l-m*|^2)  [standard Poincare log map, curvature -1]
  r <- r * min(1, R_max/|r|), R_max = atanh(0.95)
  Lorentz lift: x = ((1+|m*|^2)/(1-|m*|^2), 2m*/(1-|m*|^2)); o = (1,0,...,0)
  PT_{m*->o}(r) = r + (<o, r>_L / (1 - <x,o>_L)) * (x + o)   with <_,_>_L the Minkowski inner product
  p_{l+1} = exp_0(PT_{m*->o}(r)) = tanh(|s|) * s/|s|, s = spatial part of PT_{m*->o}(r)
  token_l = a*
  commitment/reconstruction losses unchanged from the baseline; argmaxes are straight-through.
Epoch loop: forward all training items -> hard assignments A_l -> F_l = rownorm(scatter_add(n_ij, A_l(i), A_l(j))) with add-alpha smoothing, alpha = 1/N_items, N_items = 24556, detached.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder point p_l in the Poincare ball (dim 128), codebook matrices C_l (256x128), geodesic neighbour list of order M per atom (recomputed each epoch from the same 256x256 atom distance matrix the baseline already forms), the detach

ed atom flow F_l (256x256). Outputs: SID token a* per item per level (integer, 1..256), the residual point p_{l+1} for the next level, and the standard VQ loss terms.
SAFEGUARDS: clip every ball point to norm <= 0.95 before any log map; clamp the acosh/atanh argument to 1+1e-7 for the Lorentz lift and to 1-1e-7 for the Klein inverse; if |r| is non-finite or zero, set p_{l+1} to a small fixed perturbed copy of the origin direction (fallback p_{l+1} = 0.5 * p_l) so the level does not receive a NaN; fall back to b* = a* whenever the flow row is empty, all-zero or a* is the only neighbour; deterministic tie-break by the smaller atom index in both argmin and argmax; flow matrices are detached buffers with stop_gradient; if an atom receives no assignment for an epoch, keep its previous flow row instead of zeroing it; M, alpha and R_max are fixed documented defaults (M = sqrt(|C_l|)/2, alpha = 1/N_items, R_max = atanh(0.95)) and are not swept; if more than 95% of items pick b* = a*, log it and let the run continue rather than changing constants mid-run.
END IDEA
